about.title: About Dallyletter Elidems | African Learning, Open to the World
about.description: Learn about Dallyletter Elidems, its Zimbabwe-first and internationally welcoming education technology mission, and its founder and sole creator, Elisha Maposa.
about.intro: Dallyletter Elidems is an education-technology initiative being built to bring useful learning and teaching workflows into one connected digital environment. Zimbabwe is the initial market focus, with South Africa as an important early market; learners, educators and educational organisations elsewhere are welcome.

sections.title: Why it is being built
sections.body: Learning often involves disconnected materials, assignments, communication and progress records. Dallyletter's direction is to make those activities easier to access and manage in one place, while keeping the needs of learners and educators at the centre.

sections.title: An African starting point, a global outlook
sections.body: The initial market focus is Zimbabwe and South Africa. The longer-term ambition is to support diverse African educational contexts and welcome international participation. Curriculum availability must be checked against the subjects and materials actually published on the platform; we do not claim complete coverage of every syllabus.

sections.title: Founder and authorship
sections.body: Dallyletter Elidems was founded and solely created by Elisha Maposa. The project is being developed with an emphasis on practical education workflows, transparent progress and continuous improvement.

sections.title: What we believe
sections.body: Digital education should be useful, understandable and honest about its limits. We aim to show what is available, identify what is still being improved and listen to learners, teachers and institutions before expanding claims or commitments.

learners.title: Online Learning for Learners in Zimbabwe and Beyond | Dallyletter
learners.description: Explore practical digital learning workflows with Dallyletter Elidems: lessons, practice, assignments, classes, study support and progress tools for learners.
learners.intro: Make your study time more organised. Dallyletter brings learning materials, practice, assignments and communication into a connected learner workspace, with Zimbabwe first, with South Africa and the wider African region also welcomed and an international welcome.

sections.title: Build a repeatable study routine
sections.body: Choose one topic, set a small target and return to it consistently. A useful routine is more valuable than a complicated timetable that is difficult to maintain.
bullets: Write down the topic and what you need to understand.
Study a short section, then close the notes and recall the main ideas.
Practise with questions and mark the points you could not explain.
Return to difficult ideas after a gap instead of cramming everything at once.

sections.title: Keep learning activities connected
sections.body: The learner workspace is designed to bring together lessons and media, exercises, assignments, classes, study groups, notifications and communication. Availability depends on your account role and the tools enabled for your learning space.

sections.title: Use feedback to improve
sections.body: Treat corrections as information about what to practise next. Keep a short error list, redo questions without looking at the answer and ask for clarification when an explanation is unclear.

sections.title: Start with the right next step
sections.body: Create an account to begin the learner journey, or sign in if you already have access. For navigation help, use the learner guide.

educators.title: Digital Teaching Tools for Educators | Dallyletter Elidems
educators.description: Discover Dallyletter's educator direction: lesson delivery, classes, assignments, learner engagement, feedback and connected teaching workflows.
educators.intro: Teaching involves much more than presenting content. Dallyletter is developing a connected educator workspace to support lesson delivery, class activity, assignments, learner communication and academic follow-through.

sections.title: Plan and share learning
sections.body: Use a clear lesson objective, a short explanation, an example and a task that lets learners demonstrate understanding. Digital materials work best when they are organised around what learners should be able to do.

sections.title: Connect teaching to practice
sections.body: The platform's educator workflows include lesson and class spaces, assignments, learner engagement and assessment-related tools. Use the features available to your approved account; do not assume every workflow is enabled for every school or user.

sections.title: Make feedback actionable
sections.body: Useful feedback identifies what is correct, what needs attention and what the learner should try next. Encourage learners to revisit corrected work and explain their reasoning.

sections.title: Teacher access and professional review
sections.body: Teacher registration and teaching access are distinct. Where an application or qualification review is required, complete the requested information and wait for the platform's decision before relying on teaching permissions.

schools.title: Digital Learning and School Workflows for Schools | Dallyletter Elidems
schools.description: Explore Dallyletter Elidems for schools: role-aware learner and teacher workspaces, academic oversight, attendance, records and responsible school operations.
schools.intro: Schools need tools that connect classroom activity with responsible administration. Dallyletter is being developed to support school learning communities through role-aware workspaces and connected academic and operational workflows.

sections.title: Role-aware workspaces
sections.body: Different people need different levels of access. Learners, teachers, managers and platform owners should see only the workspaces and actions permitted for their accounts.

sections.title: Academic operations
sections.body: The platform includes workflows for classes, lessons, attendance, learner records, assignments and review activity. The exact availability of each workflow should be confirmed during an institutional discussion and tested in the relevant environment.

sections.title: Staff and learner administration
sections.body: Teacher applications, qualifications and transfer-related reviews are intended to follow controlled review processes. Approval authority and access should remain limited to appropriately authorised accounts.

sections.title: Fees and payment visibility
sections.body: Financial workflows depend on the institution's configured fee rules and the payment providers enabled for its account. Do not treat a learner's payment notification as proof of settlement; verified transaction status is the source of truth.

sections.title: Start a conversation
sections.body: School leaders can discuss institutional scope, access, support and commercial terms with authorised platform administration. No unverified partnership, accreditation or price is implied.

resources.title: Study Resources and Practical Learning Guides | Dallyletter
resources.description: Read practical study guidance from Dallyletter Elidems: active recall, spaced practice, weekly planning, assignment habits and exam preparation.
resources.intro: Good study advice should be specific enough to use today. This resource hub focuses on practical habits learners can apply across subjects, schools and learning environments.

sections.title: Study with active recall
sections.body: After reading a section, put the notes aside and write or say what you remember. Check the source, correct gaps and repeat. Recalling information strengthens understanding more than repeatedly rereading without testing yourself.

sections.title: Space your practice
sections.body: Return to important material over several days. Short sessions separated by time help reveal what you can remember independently and what still needs work.

sections.title: Turn assignments into steps
sections.body: Read the task, identify the deliverable, list the smaller actions, start with the first action and check the final work against the instructions before submitting.

sections.title: Plan a realistic week
sections.body: A useful plan includes specific topics, manageable study blocks, breaks and time to revisit difficult questions. Leave room for school, family responsibilities and unexpected changes.

study-plan.title: A Simple 7-Day Study Plan for Learners | Dallyletter
study-plan.description: Use this practical seven-day study plan to organise topics, practise recall, solve questions and review difficult areas without last-minute cramming.
study-plan.intro: A study plan should help you start, not make you feel behind. Use this seven-day framework for one subject or one topic, then adapt the time and workload to your real schedule.

sections.title: Day 1 — Choose a clear target
sections.body: Write the topic, the reason it matters and three questions you want to be able to answer by the end of the week. Gather the notes and learning materials you need.

sections.title: Day 2 — Understand the foundations
sections.body: Study one small section. Explain it in your own words and write down any terms or steps you cannot yet explain.

sections.title: Day 3 — Practise without looking
sections.body: Close your notes and answer questions from memory. Check your answers and record mistakes without judging yourself.

sections.title: Day 4 — Fix the gaps
sections.body: Return to the two or three ideas that caused difficulty. Find another explanation or example, then try a fresh question.

sections.title: Day 5 — Mix and apply
sections.body: Combine questions from earlier sections. Explain why each method or answer is appropriate, not only what the answer is.

sections.title: Day 6 — Complete a short check
sections.body: Set a reasonable time limit and complete a small practice set. Review accuracy, understanding and the questions that took longest.

sections.title: Day 7 — Review and plan forward
sections.body: Summarise what improved, list remaining gaps and choose the next topic. Keep the plan flexible enough to fit your school and home responsibilities.

organisations.title: Digital Learning Partnerships for Educational Organisations | Dallyletter Elidems
organisations.description: Explore Dallyletter Elidems for tutoring centres, community learning programmes, education providers and training organisations. Review learner support, role-aware workflows and responsible onboarding.
organisations.intro: Dallyletter Elidems is being developed for organisations that coordinate learning beyond a single classroom — including tutoring centres, community programmes, education providers and training teams. Zimbabwe is the initial market focus, with South Africa as an important early market; organisations elsewhere are welcome to discuss whether the platform fits their needs.

sections.title: Who this is for
sections.body: This pathway is for teams that organise learning across groups, programmes or locations. Examples include tutoring and extra lessons centres, community education initiatives, non-profit learning programmes, private education providers and skills or training organisations. A conversation should establish whether the current platform capabilities fit the organisation's actual work.
bullets: Tutoring centres coordinating tutors, learners and learning groups.
Community or non-profit programmes supporting structured learning.
Education providers managing multiple cohorts or learning services.
Training teams delivering lessons, practice and learner follow-up.

sections.title: Coordinate learning programmes
sections.body: Dallyletter's direction is to connect learning materials, lessons, assignments, communication and learner progress in one environment. The exact workflows available depend on the organisation's approved account, enabled features and configured learning space; confirm each required workflow before onboarding.

sections.title: Keep access and learner information responsible
sections.body: Different staff members need different access. Role-aware workspaces and individually authorised actions are intended to keep learner information and operational decisions within appropriate boundaries. Organisations should agree who can view records, communicate with learners and approve administrative actions before a programme begins.

sections.title: Make fees and payment status clear
sections.body: Any fee or payment workflow depends on the fee rules configured by authorised platform administration and the payment providers enabled for the account. A learner's self-reported payment is not proof of settlement; use verified transaction status and agree how partial payments, balances and receipts will be handled.

sections.title: Plan a practical onboarding conversation
sections.body: Before starting, confirm the programme's learner groups, curriculum or subject needs, staff roles, privacy expectations, support arrangements, required workflows and commercial terms. No price, partnership, accreditation or guaranteed outcome is implied by this information page.
